newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to keep real interest rates high - Belka.
newsitem.headline: Poland to keep real interest rates high - Belka.

text.p: Poland's finance minister said on Wednesday that the central bank is likely to keep its real interest rates high and is likely to cut nominal rates only if credit action is curbed.

"We have to take into account that a high level of interest rates in real terms will be maintained. This does not mean that nominal levels will not be lowered at some point," the minister, Marek Belka, told a news conference.
The independent National Bank of Poland keeps real interest rates high to curb fast growing credit. Recent credit expansion has prompted fears that the Polish economy may be overheating.

The NBP's market rates are now at 22.0-22.15 percent against year-on-year inflation of 15.3 percent in April. The nominal rates are at 22.0 and 25.0 percent. Inflation is seen falling to 13 percent in year-on-year terms in December.
Belka said the central bank was likely to consider a nominal rate cut only when credit growth is reduced, but that even after a nominal rate cut real rates would stay high.
"When the pace of credit growth is significantly curbed and is relatively sustained, we think the central bank will react," he said.
Credit grew 12.1 percent since the start of the year against savings growth of 6.5 percent and broad money supply growth of 7.9 percent in that period.
Poland wants to curb credit expansion to cool domestic demand and diminish its fast rising trade gap, which is seen rising to 3-3.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from one percent in 1996.
